title: Replace a Bathtub Drum Trap with PVC P-Trap (This Old House)
summary: This Old House demonstrates replacing an aging bathtub drum trap with a modern PVC P-trap. The speaker explains that the trap provides a water seal to prevent sewer gas from entering the tub, introduces the self-scouring feature of the P-trap, and walks through removing the old trap, disconnecting the threaded adapter, selecting appropriate adapters, and sealing old-work joints with pipe dope and wick. The process includes dry-fitting, taking a measurement to cut, deburring, cleaning, and gluing the PVC joints, while marking alignment witness marks to ensure the correct angles. The lesson emphasizes careful preparation and fit before final assembly, with practical notes on tools and joint sealing techniques.

sections.title: Trap function and plan to replace with PVC P-trap
sections.description: Explain that the tub drain passes through a trap that creates a water seal to keep sewer gas out, and introduce the plan to replace the old drum trap with a modern, self-scouring PVC P-trap.

sections.title: Remove old drum trap and prepare for PVC replacement
sections.description: Remove the existing trap assembly and prepare for installing a PVC alternative.

sections.title: Disconnect old threaded adapter and plan new connections
sections.description: Work to remove the threaded adapter with tools and discuss sealing methods for threaded joints, including pipe dope and wick.

sections.title: Dry-fit and measure for cut
sections.description: Dry-fit the PVC pieces and determine the measurement needed to cut, planning for a secure fit with a 3-inch clip.

sections.title: Deburr and prep interior of fittings
sections.description: Deburr cut ends to prevent catching hair and ensure a clean insertion path.

sections.title: Glue, marks, and alignment for PVC joints
sections.description: Mark alignment lines on fittings and pipe to ensure proper orientation when gluing; test-fit the 90-degree elbow and align pieces before applying adhesive.

sections.title: Final assembly check and closing aside
sections.description: Conclude the assembly and share a light aside about the plumber, noting the job completion.
